newsitem.title: USA: MESA Inc closes Greenhill acquisition.
newsitem.headline: MESA Inc closes Greenhill acquisition.

text.p: MESA Inc said on Thursday that it has acquired Greenhill Petroleum Corp from Australia's WMC Ltd for $267 million.
With the completion of this major acquisition, MESA will immediately begin development and exploration activities on the properties, MESA said.
As of the end of 1996, Greenhill's estimated proved reserves include approximately 23 million barrels of oil and condensate and 42 billion cubic feet of gas, MESA said.
As a result of this transaction, the percentage of MESA's total reserves from oil and condensate will increase from approximately 3 percent to approximately 10 percent.

MESA's estimated proved reserves and the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows before income taxes, after giving pro forma effect to the Greenhill acquisition, as of Dec. 31, 1996, were 1.8 trillion cubic feet of natural gas equivalents and $2.1 billion, respectively, the company said.
Greenhill's production for the year ended Dec. 31, 1996 was 6 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 2.5 million barrels of oil, MESA said.

After giving pro forma effect to the Greenhill acquisition, MESA's 1996 production was 90 billion cubic feet of gas, 6.5 million barrels of natural gas liquids and 3.4 million barrels of oil and condensate, MESA said.

MESA, which announced last week merger plans with Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co, said it will operate over 90 percent of the Greenhill properties, which are concentrated in the inland waters of Louisiana, the Texas Gulf Coast, the Gulf of Mexico and the Permian Basin.
The acquired properties include 522 producing wells, over 200 development projects and 246 square miles of 3-D seismic data, MESA said.

MESA's exploitation plans for 1997 include spending $36 million of its $130 million 1997 capital budget on 44 development projects on the Greenhill properties, with another 25 projects it expects to initiate in 1998, it said.
